name: AFAC (Australian and New Zealand Council for Fire and Emergency Services)
scale_note: Member-based council whose fire, emergency service and land management member agencies lead a paid and volunteer workforce of more than 288,000 people

name: After the Fire USA
scale_note: Initiative of Rebuild North Bay Foundation; brings recovery knowledge from 15+ fires and helped deliver over $6 billion in tax relief for disaster survivors

name: AGIF (Agency for the Integrated Management of Rural Fires)
scale_note: Public institute responsible for planning, strategic coordination and evaluation of Portugal's Integrated Rural Fire Management System (SGIFR), a multi-institutional system of 12 entities

name: ALERTCalifornia
scale_note: Over 1,200 high-definition pan-tilt-zoom cameras deployed across California as of February 2026; operated by UC San Diego

name: BlazeAid
scale_note: 100% volunteer-based charity rebuilding fences and clearing debris with families after bushfires, floods and cyclones; 10 camps currently active across Australia

name: California Fire Safe Council
scale_note: Sacramento-based nonprofit supporting a network of local fire safe councils across California through grant funding, programmatic support and technical assistance

name: Canada Wildfire (Canadian Partnership for Wildland Fire Science)
scale_note: NSERC Strategic Network hosted at the University of Alberta; research on fire behavior, ecology and risk assessment

name: Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre (CIFFC)
scale_note: Not-for-profit corporation coordinating resource sharing, mutual aid and information sharing among Canadian federal, provincial and territorial wildland fire agencies

name: Cultural Fire Management Council
scale_note: Community-based nonprofit facilitating cultural burning on the Yurok Reservation and ancestral lands; programs include Family Burns, TREX, fuels reduction and cooperative burns

name: Earth Fire Alliance
scale_note: First three operational FireSat satellites reached orbit in July 2026; constellation developed with input from 200+ firefighters and scientists; $26M Bezos Earth Fund grant (June 2026)

name: European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS)
scale_note: Part of EU Copernicus Emergency Management Services since 2015; expert network spans 43 countries; European Fire Database holds nearly 2 million records from 22 countries

name: Fire Adapted Communities Learning Network (FAC Net)
scale_note: Connects fire adapted community leaders around the United States to increase wildfire resilience

name: Fire Networks
scale_note: Umbrella for four peer networks active across the United States: Fire Learning Network, Fire Adapted Communities Learning Network, Indigenous Peoples Burning Network, and Prescribed Fire Training Exchanges (TREX)

name: FireHawk
scale_note: Site states it monitors approximately 14 million hectares of forestry across Africa and South America through continuous camera-tower and satellite detection with expert verification.

name: First Nations' Emergency Services Society of British Columbia (FNESS)
scale_note: Partners with First Nations across British Columbia on emergency management, including wildfire mitigation and a Forest Fuels Management department; offices in Kamloops and Vancouver

name: Fundacion Reforestemos
scale_note: Over 1.7 million native trees planted; recovery and restoration work across 12 regions in Chile with expansion to Argentina and Peru; 700+ corporate partners

name: Global Fire Monitoring Center (GFMC)
scale_note: Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany (with a second headquarters in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia); coordinates 14 Regional Wildland Fire Networks and eight regional centers covering all continents

name: Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS)
scale_note: Run by the European Commission Joint Research Centre; provides global fire danger forecasting, active fire detection, burnt area mapping and emissions analysis

name: International Association of Wildland Fire (IAWF)
scale_note: 501(c)(3) professional association representing members of the global wildland fire community

name: Living Knowledge Network (formerly Firesticks Alliance Indigenous Corporation)
scale_note: Community-led Indigenous network described as the next chapter of Firesticks, extending cultural burning into broader Indigenous Knowledge Systems work

name: National Aerial Firefighting Centre (NAFC)
scale_note: Business unit of AFAC coordinating a national fleet of approximately 150 contracted firefighting aircraft shared by Australian states and territories

name: National Forest Foundation
scale_note: 501(c)(3) partner of the U.S. Forest Service reforesting acres damaged by wildfire; over 50 million trees planted since 2001 across 81 forests in 31 states

name: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC)
scale_note: Multi-agency wildland fire coordination campus in Boise, Idaho; approximately 650 year-round employees, roughly 1,000 during peak fire season

name: OroraTech
scale_note: States 800+ users in 25 countries, 170+ employees across 5 continents, monitoring of 500 million hectares, and 35+ combined satellite sources feeding its wildfire platform.

name: Pantau Gambut
scale_note: NGO network across nine provinces of Indonesia; tracks peatland fire hotspots using LAPAN satellite data

name: Pau Costa Foundation
scale_note: Foundation based in Taradell, Barcelona connecting the fire community, research and society; projects span the Mediterranean, Colombia, Northern Ireland and tropical regions

name: Pyregence Consortium
scale_note: Open wildfire science consortium formed through a California Energy Commission EPIC grant; PyreCast platform offers fire forecasts up to 16 days in advance

name: Satellites on Fire
scale_note: Reported to have covered 21 countries and helped manage more than 600 fires in Latin America in one year, with over 55,000 users and 20,000 field-validated wildfire reports, per ImpactAlpha.

name: Satellites on Fire
scale_note: Site states 55,000 users across 21 countries, roughly 95 fires assisted per month, and a validated database of over 90,000 fire events across 15 Latin American countries; claims detection 20 minutes ahead of any public satellite system.

name: Watch Duty
scale_note: 501(c)(3) nonprofit; describes itself as the fire tracking app used by millions, with coverage across the United States

name: WIFIRE Program (Societal Computing and Innovation Lab, UC San Diego)
scale_note: Fire modeling and management initiative hosted at the San Diego Supercomputer Center, UC San Diego
